content:
You should first verify your server settings. Here are my working Comcast settings:

IMAP (Incoming): Incoming Server Type: IMAP Mail Server Incoming Server Name: imap.comcast.net Port: 993 User Name: <my email address> Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: Normal Password OR OAuth2

SMTP (Outgoing): SMTP Server Name: smtp.comcast.net Port: 465 Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: Normal Password OR OAuth2 User Name: <my email address>

I use IMAP but if your incoming server is POP3, you would use this:

POP3 (Incoming): Incoming Server Type: POP Mail Server Incoming Server Name: pop3.comcast.net Port: 995 User Name: <email address> Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: Normal Password (or OAuth2?)

These are the same as what Comcast recommends (see https://www.xfinity.com/support/articles/email-client-programs-with-xfinity-email) except they don't mention using OAuth2 as the Authentication Method. OAuth2 is better, but the older, less-secure Normal Password method may still work.

To make OAuth2 work properly in Thunderbird you must make sure that cookies are allowed (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Accept Cookies from Sites>.) You should also delete any existing Comcast entries in Saved Passwords (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Passwords | Saved Passwords>.) Then, restart Thunderbird. You will be prompted for your credentials and you should be authenticated.

content:
A couple things to try:

- The Sent folder's index might be corrupt. To Repair it, right-click on the folder name and choose "Properties" from the pop-up context menu, then "Repair folder." Follow this with by Compacting the folder (choose "Compact Folder" from the same context menu.)

- A slightly more brute-force way of accomplishing a similar result: from the account name in the Folders List, right-click and choose "Subscribe". You will be presented with a list of all your Gmail IMAP folders. Deselect "Sent" or "Sent Mail" from the list and click "OK". The Sent folder will disappear from your folders list. Now, go back to Subscribe and re-enable "Sent Mail". The folder will reappear and download all your Sent mail again, and hopefully it will update properly.

content:
All of your accounts, messages, folders, preferences, etc. are stored in your Profile. The default location of your Thunderbird Profile is <C:\Users\(your Windows account)\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird>. This folder can contain multiple profiles if you have them. This is separate from the actual program folder.

Profiles are forward-compatible but not necessarily backward-compatible. That is, a Profile created by an older version can be happily used by a newer version. The newer version may change the format of some of its files, so it may no longer be able to be used by an older version. You may have to make a few tweaks, and you might have to re-authenticate your accounts, but in general things should work pretty much as they did before.

It's safest to keep an intact copy of your Profile somewhere handy until you have completed the migration, in case something goes wrong. Even after that, it's best practice to make regular backups of that folder if your email store is precious to you.

It sounds like you already found the method of transferring a profile from one computer to another. If you would like help with that, ask here or start a new thread.
